News.title: At least 10 dead and a dozen missing after packed boat crashes into bridge and capsizes sparking frantic rescue mission
News.content:
BOAT HORROR At least 10 dead and a dozen missing after packed boat crashes into bridge and capsizes sparking frantic rescue mission

AT LEAST ten people have died after a boat carrying around 30 passengers capsized in India.

The overcrowded vessel overturned on the Yamuna River near Keshighat in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh.





Rescue teams including local police, fire services, divers, and boatmen pulled 14 survivors from the water.

At least twelve passengers remain missing, according to authorities.

Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) have now piled into the frantic search.

Horrified witnesses reported that the boat struck the pontoon bridge before capsizing.

Mathura DIG Shailesh Kumar Pandey said the crash “appears to be the primary reason for the accident.”

The passengers had travelled from Punjab, according to officials.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said rescue and relief efforts “must be accelerated”, and the injured “should receive urgent aid”.

A video taken moments before the catastrophe shows passengers packed in together without life jackets.



Law enforcement officials have initiated an enquiry.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he was “deeply pained” by news of the incident.

He said: “My condolences to those who have lost their near and dear ones. I pray for the speedy recovery of the injured.”

As divers continue to scour the river, authorities have urged caution and pledged to strengthen safety measures along the Yamuna.

Breaking News… More to Come…

News.title: Two teens dead after car plunges off M1 bridge and crashes into minibus below
News.content:
BRIDGE HORROR Two teens dead after car plunges off M1 bridge and crashes into minibus below

TWO teenagers have died after a car crashed off a bridge and hit a minibus on the motorway below, police have confirmed.

Emergency services scrambled to the scene on the M1 around junction 20 in Leicestershire yesterday afternoon.





Four people were travelling in the minibus – Fiat Ducato – and were taken to hospital following the incident, reported at 1.33pm.

The teens were in a blue car driving along Gilmorton Lane, towards Lutterworth.

The route remained closed into the night, with huge queues of vehicles snaking back miles.



Leicestershire Police said: “Two people have died following a road traffic collision on the M1 southbound shortly before junction 20.

“Police were called at 1.33pm this afternoon following a report that a blue car, travelling along Gilmorton Lane towards Lutterworth, had left the road bridge above the carriageway and collided with a minibus travelling southbound on the M1.

“Leicestershire Fire and Rescue Service and East Midlands Ambulance Service also attended the scene.

“Four people in the minibus – a white Fiat Ducato – were taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. The driver, a man, has been discharged and three women remain in hospital.



“The two people in the blue car, both teenagers, were declared dead at the scene.

“The road is likely to remain closed for a number of hours yet while forensic work continues to be carried out.

“Leicestershire Police would like to hear from anyone who was driving on Gilmorton Lane or on the M1 in the area of junction 20 – in both directions – at around 1.30pm on Friday afternoon.

“Anyone with dashcam footage or who car either vehicle before the collision is asked to contact us.

“Please contact us on 101, quoting incident number 308 of 10th April or visit Making a road traffic incident report | Leicestershire Police.”

News.title: Terrifying moment hooded yobs slash machetes at each other in town centre as bystanders left horrified & cops scramble
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a gang of machete wielding yobs brawled on a busy high street in broad daylight.

Terrified shoppers watched on as the horror unfolded on Foundry Street in Dewsbury town centre, West Yorkshire.





Video footage from the scene captured the knife fight during the confrontation on Friday.

A shocked onlooker nearby filmed the blade battle on their mobile phone.

The thugs freely brandished their weapons on the busy high street as stunned bystanders walked past.



At least four of the thugs were seen wielding large blades as they faced off against another yob in a balaclava.

The masked individual even picked up a trolley bag in self-defence as the fight moved down the street.

Violence then erupts as one of the thugs lunges forward with his blade.

The balaclava-clad yob manages to block the blows but is soon set upon by the gang of armed thugs.



He manages to block a few strikes despite stumbling backwards.

Dressed in a black balaclava, he regains his footing and is seen backing away during the footage.

Gobsmacked bystanders can be seen watching on as the brawl occurred in broad daylight.

One of the yobs carrying a large machete was captured posturing towards a person filming and even lunged towards them during the shocking footage.

The thug, dressed in a black coat with navy hoodie on underneath, was with two other males who also wielded dangerous machete-style knives.



Frightened witnesses dialled 999 following the horror yesterday.

A police helicopter was seen circling overhead as armed officers rushed to the scene.

The are currently no reports of any injuries or arrests, said cops.

West Yorkshire police said: ”At 3.27pm officers were called to Foundry Street in Dewsbury to reports people were fighting in the street with machetes.”

“Armed Police attended, all was in order and no injuries have been reported.



“Enquiries are ongoing.”

News.title: Labour must avoid ‘bloody’ leadership war after local elections, warns deputy leader
News.content:
LABOUR’S deputy leader has warned plotters not to drag the party into a “bloody” leadership war after next month’s local elections.

Lucy Powell said any move to oust Sir Keir Starmer would go down badly with members – especially with the Iran crisis still raging.



She blasted the idea of a leadership challenge as a “messy, bloody internal contest” that would do nothing to steady the country.



The Manchester Central MP told The Financial Times: “I’ve got my own job and my own mandate.

“I’m not saying this because I want to suck up to anyone. I’m saying it because it’s the right thing for the party and country.

“Some kind of messy, bloody internal contest is not going to help us address these issues.

“I think the membership would take a very dim view of that.”



The Deputy Leader also said the PM’s handling of the Iran war is winning the “biggest clap” at party events.

Ms Powell added: “We need calm, sensible, grown-up leadership to take us through this.”

Her comments come as nerves grow in Labour ranks over the looming local elections.

Party insiders fear a bruising night, with predictions of heavy losses driven by the rise of Reform and the Greens.



There are also warnings Labour could be wiped out in Wales and slump to third or even fourth in Scotland.

Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar has already piled pressure on the PM, calling for him to quit amid the Peter Mandelson scandal earlier this year.

News.title: Woman, 24, slipped and fell to her death from bridge following row with boyfriend after work Christmas party
News.content:
PLUNGE TRAGEDY Woman, 24, slipped and fell to her death from bridge following row with boyfriend after work Christmas party

A 24-YEAR-OLD woman died after falling from a bridge following a row with her boyfriend at a work Christmas party, an inquest heard.

Emma Bundy had climbed over safety railings on a pedestrian overbridge on the A379 near Sandy Park in Exeter, Devon, where a member of the public desperately tried to save her.





The hearing at Exeter Coroner’s Court was told Emma, an assistant site manager with Bovis Homes, had been attending a delayed work Christmas party at the Sandy Park conference venue at the end of January 2025.

During the evening, she became upset following a disagreement with her boyfriend, Billy Fleming, linked to something said by a colleague.

She then left the venue and headed towards the bridge, with Mr Fleming following behind.

Motorist George Harris, who had been waiting nearby to collect his daughter from the event, saw Emma in distress near the bridge.



He said Mr Fleming returned alone shortly afterwards and, when asked if Emma was alright, described her as being “off her head”.

Concerned, Mr Harris went to look for Emma and found her clinging to the outside of the bridge, holding on with her hands.

He called emergency services and tried to help, holding onto her wrists and urging her to keep hold.

Mr Harris told the court she was crying and extremely distressed.



Despite his efforts over several minutes, Emma slipped from his grasp and fell onto the road below.

She died from injuries to her chest and neck.

Mr Fleming had returned to his hotel room before the tragic fall, but was later informed by police of what had taken place.

He described Emma as “‘beautiful, kind hearted and would move mountains for anyone”.

Police have said there are no suspicious circumstances surrounding her death and the coroner ruled it an accident.



Toxicology reports found that Emma had alcohol in her system when she died, and that it likely affected her judgement.

Senior Devon coroner, Philip Spinney, said: “She did not intentionally end her life. She was trying to stop herself from falling.

“It is unclear how she came to be on the wrong side of the safety barriers and was trying to stop herself falling.

“She was upset at something a work colleague had said earlier that evening.”

“It is more likely than not she acted impulsively and did not intend to end her life, this was a tragic accident.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The assistant site manager was well praised within the industry, having turned her life around after facing homelessness.

She has previously spoken out about her gratitude for her job, including the levels of support she received.

News.title: New pics of the ‘Arc de Trump’ reveal huge 250 foot triumphal arch in Washington DC as towering white monument
News.content:
DON-UMENT DOCS New pics of the ‘Arc de Trump’ reveal huge 250 foot triumphal arch in Washington DC as towering white monument

NEW pictures have revealed Donald Trump’s proposed massive triumphal arch that could be a feature of Washington DC.

The Interior Department has submitted the renders for the plans of the arch slated to be located near Arlington National Cemetery.





The proposal shows the arch would be an estimated 250 feet tall – more than twice the height of the 99-foot tall Lincoln Memorial just across the Potomac River.

The plans would make it the tallest triumphal arch in the world – just as the president said he wanted.

It would measure as around 30 feet taller than the Plaza de La Republica in Mexico City.



Trump posted to his social media platform Truth Social about the plans on Friday.

“I am pleased to announce that TODAY my Administration officially filed the presentation and plans to the highly respected Commission of Fine Arts for what will be the GREATEST and MOST BEAUTIFUL Triumphal Arch, anywhere in the World,” he wrote.

“This will be a wonderful addition to the Washington D.C. area for all Americans to enjoy for many decades to come!”

The proposed site would place the arch in the centre of a traffic circle on the Virginia side of the Potomac – between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.



The land technically falls within the boundaries of the District of Columbia.

Inscriptions reading “One Nation Under God” and “Liberty and Justice for All” are planned to be carved into either side of the arch.

A gold-coloured Lady Liberty flanked by two eagles is planned to top the structure, with four statues of lions guarding the base.

The designs were prepared by Harrison Design, an architecture firm in Washington.

Friday’s submission is the first time the Trump administration has officially entered plans for the arch, which the president has boasted about for months.



“I’d like it to be the biggest one of all,” Trump told reporters in January.

“We’re the biggest, most powerful nation.”

Actively endorsing the project, Trump has shared the design concepts over the last several months, saying the arch was for “me”.

“It’s going to be beautiful.”

The arch – which resembles Paris’ Arc de Triomphe – will commemorate the country’s 250th anniversary, according to Trump.



Its construction will be funded by American taxpayers, as per the spending plan for the National Endowment for the Humanities released by the Trump administration earlier this week.

The spending plan – which was approved by the Office of Management and Budget in September last year – shows that $2 million (£1.49 million) in special initiative funds and $13 million (£9.66 million) in matching funds have been “reserved for the arch”.

But the proposed site is along a flight path for the nearby Reagan National Airport – raising questions about how it would affect planes approaching the major airfield.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Commission of Fine Arts, a panel composed entirely of Trump appointees, is set to hear a presentation about the arch on April 16.

News.title: Boy, 9, ‘locked in van by dad’ for over a year & forced to poo in bin bags as he’s left unable to walk after rescue
News.content:
CRUEL FATHER Boy, 9, ‘locked in van by dad’ for over a year & forced to poo in bin bags as he’s left unable to walk after rescue

A NINE-YEAR-OLD boy has been rescued after allegedly being locked in a van for more than a year by his dad, forced to poo in bin bags.

The child was unable to walk after so long in cramped conditions in the vehicle in Hagenbach, eastern France.



He was found on Monday and told cops he had been shut in the van since the end of 2024, when he was just seven.



When cops arrived to the car park where the van was kept, he told them that he couldn’t open the van because of a jammed locking system.

Police were shocked at what they found inside.

The boy was naked under a blanket in horrifying conditions after neighbours said they heard “sounds of a child” coming from the van.

Police said the boy was found “lying in the foetal position, naked, covered by a blanket on a pile of rubbish, close to human excrement”.

The boy told cops he was not even allowed to leave the van to go to the toilet – he had been forced to wee in bottles and poo in bin bags.

They added that he was malnourished and unable to walk after being trapped in the vehicle for so long.

When neighbours first raised the alarm, they were told the sound was just a cat.

The child’s 43-year-old dad was arrested and his other children – two girls, aged 10 and 12 – were taken into care.



He told cops that his 37-year-old partner hadn’t wanted the child in the flat, telling him to send him to a psychiatric hospital.

He said he shut him in the vehicle to “protect him” and avoid sending him away, but told neighbours and friends he had put the boy into care.

Police said the last time the boy had had a shower was in 2024.

The boy told police that his dad would leave him bottles of water and brought him food twice a day.

He was briefly allowed to return to the flat last summer, while the rest of his family were on holiday – his dad gave him a phone at this point “to communicate with him and tell him when he could get out of the van or when he had to leave the apartment”.



The boy had a stellar school record and prosecutors said there was “no medical evidence” to suggest that he had any psychiatric problems.

CCTV showed the dad going to the van twice a day “where he appeared to be throwing something inside”.

The dad said his partner had no idea he had locked the child in the van.

She said she was convinced the child had been taken to a psychiatric hospital – but admitted to hearing noises from the van.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The dad was charged on Wednesday with arrest, abduction, confinement, or arbitrary detention of a child and depriving food or care to a child.



His partner was charged with failure to report mistreatment, deprivation, assault, or sexual abuse inflicted on a minor under 15 years of age.

News.title: Baby-faced far-right politician tipped to be next French president dates Italian princess despite railing against elites
News.content:
UNLIKELY LOVE Baby-faced far-right politician tipped to be next French president dates Italian princess despite railing against elites

A FAR-right politician tipped to be the next French president has revealed he is in a relationship with an Italian princess despite years of campaigning against elites.

Jordan Bardella, 30, leader of the National Rally (RN) political party dropped the news of his bombshell romance with Maria Carolina of Bourbon-Two Sicilies, 22, this week.





Following months of speculation, the couple appeared together on the cover of French pop-culture magazine Paris Match on April 9.

Appearing in candid portraits in the magazine, the couple has unveiled their union with the carefully orchestrated announcement.

Whispers of the couple’s romance have been flying since the beginning of the year, when they were filmed together walking down the steps of the Grand Palais in Paris.

They had been attending the bicentenary of Le Figaro.

Previously, Bardella has refused to comment on the relationship, saying his “private life” was his “last bastion of freedom”.

However, he never denied the rumour.

Carolina is the descendant of a prestigious and extremely wealthy Italian aristocratic family.



The shock announcement comes after the nationalist MEP refused to comment on his relationship amid a media frenzy.

“Until further notice, my private life belongs to me,” he said in an interview on RTL Radio at the end of January.

He had, however, described himself as a “happy man” when asked about his love life.

Days later, he spoke to Le Parisien, where he said he intended to “preserve [his privacy] as much as possible”.

National Rally MP Sébastien Chenu wished Bardella “much happiness” on the “beautiful story”, while revealing nothing else about the couple’s relationship.



Critics say the politician has finally given the public a peek into his private life ahead of the presidential election.

Dubbed as Marine Le Pen‘s protege, Bardella is set to be a front-runner in the 2027 polls, if Le Pen is deemed ineligible to run by the Court of Appeal in July.

Sharing his relationship could be a campaign tactic, as the public expects greater transparency from the politicians seeking their votes, Madame Figaro reported.

But revealing his relationship has also shed light on his connection with the Duchess of Palermo and Calabria – risking criticism from working-class voters.

National Rally politicians have come to Bardella’s defence in the face of the naysayers.



MP Alexandre Loubet said the negative comments were a “military stance [that] reeks of social contempt”.

Another National Rally MP Pierre-Romain Thionnet also commented on the backlash, characterising the headlines as “hateful and obsessive attacks” from certain journalists.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bardella was previously in a relationship with Nolwenn Olivier – Le Pen’s niece – between 2020 and 2023.

News.title: Heart-wrenching story of dog Laika who was sent into space but never returned home
News.content:
Heart-wrenching story of dog Laika who was sent into space but never returned home

The Soviet stray dog named Laika became one of the first animals in space when she was launched aboard Sputnik 2 in 1957, but the heartbreaking mission was always one-way

View 3 Images Laika was found roaming the streets of Moscow and was thought to be three-years-old (Image: AFP Contributor, AFP via Getty Images)

The heartbreaking story of Laika, the dog launched into space to orbit the Earth with no way home, has lately caused new grief online. Laika, a mixed breed from Russia, was simply one of many animals used in the tireless pursuit of human knowledge, as we strive to explore uncharted territories for a greater understanding of the universe.

‌



Despite the small dog's distinctive position as among the first animals in space, it provided scant solace as she blasted away from Earth, the sole passenger aboard the Sputnik 2 spacecraft.

‌



The unsuspecting young pup, found roaming the streets of Moscow, was thought to be just three-years-old. Her gentle, affable nature led scientists to consider her a perfect candidate for their experiment.

‌



On November 3, 1957, following weeks of preparation that included adapting her to progressively smaller crates and cages, she was sent into low orbit.

At that point, there was limited understanding about the effects of space travel on living creatures, and animal flights were regarded by engineers as an essential stepping stone to human missions.

View 3 Images Laika was amongst the first animals in space aboard the Sputnik 2 spacecraft (Image: UIG via Getty Images)

‌



Once the little stray was located, Soviet staff gave her multiple names including Kudryavka, Russian for 'Little Curly', Limonchik translating to 'Little Lemon', and Zhuchka, meaning 'Little Bug'.

Laika, the Russian word for certain breeds resembling the husky, was the name that gained recognition worldwide.

The experiment aimed to demonstrate a living creature could withstand the traumatic forces associated with launching into orbit. Laika's vital signs were meticulously monitored in the hope of confirming scientists' theories that life could function in space amid reduced gravity and elevated radiation levels.

‌



The data from her revealed indicators of distress and increased agitation throughout her voyage. Over five months after launch, Sputnik 2 - together with Laika's remains - descended back through Earth's atmosphere on April 14, 1958, incinerating upon re-entry. From this mission, researchers obtained groundbreaking information about the physiological effects of space travel through their work with Laika.

It was believed her on-board death occurred due to the central R‐7 sustainer's failure to separate from the spacecraft. The Soviet Union allegedly provided contradictory accounts concerning her death, including claims she died merely seven hours into her mission.

View 3 Images In 2002, the circumstances of Laika's death were found and that she died after using her oxygen supply (Image: UIG via Getty Images)

‌



Nevertheless, in 2002, the actual circumstances and timing of her death were ultimately disclosed, reflecting extensive reporting that she died after exhausting her oxygen supply on her sixth isolated day aboard the cramped spacecraft.

Laika's tale re-emerged across social media, spotlighted once again by the popular page, Fantastic Things in the World. Alongside an image of a statue resembling Laika looking out from the spacecraft, the user behind the account wrote: "Every year... I feel compelled to tell this story and possibly do it with new words. There's a deep guilt that all of us should feel reading what we did to Laika. Human progress has often been achieved at the expense of animals that had nothing to do with our desire for supremacy.

"Many people believe this was an acceptable price for our conquests, but it seems obvious, even reading this story, that it was really just a trivial form of prevarication." The tribute concluded: "We had a duty to choose another path. We still have that duty today. Sorry humanity has failed you, Laika."

‌



This follows as Artemis II broke its radio silence with four historic words as it emerged from the Moon.

Orion emerged from behind the Moon right on schedule, with radio contact instantly restored – bringing to an end a tense 40-minute blackout which had left Mission Control waiting in complete silence.

Mission specialist Christina Koch was the first to speak. Her first four words were: "Houston, Integrity, comm check." She then added: "It is so great to hear from Earth again."

Article continues below

With no signal possible on the lunar far side, the capsule had been operating entirely independently. Computers aboard Orion fired the engines at precisely the right moment to propel the spacecraft onto a homeward trajectory – a manoeuvre carried out well beyond the reach of any ground controller.

Today, the crew reached its closest point to the Moon and will now head back towards Earth. The four astronauts became the furthest-flying humans in history, breaking the record of Apollo 13 set in 1970.

News.title: 'I pulled up floorboards during home renovation and discovered huge issue'
News.content:
'I pulled up floorboards during home renovation and discovered huge issue'

One woman was left stunned after pulling up floorboards in her newly purchased home, hoping to find stylish tiles underneath - only to discover something much different

View Image A woman wasn't impressed by what she found under her laminate flooring (stock) (Image: Lex20 via Getty Images)

A woman who recently bought her first property and began renovation work straight away has shared her frustration after pulling up the existing laminate flooring. Kim Ladd took to TikTok to showcase her unfortunate find, after admitting she had hoped to discover attractive tiling beneath.

‌



However, what she found in reality proved to be something considerably different. "Definitely going to keep it," Kim remarked in a clip, before highlighting that it was in fact "wet concrete" underneath. This prompted numerous TikTok users to offer guidance to potential buyers on resolving the problem to prevent additional harm to her property's foundations.

‌



"This is why homeowners need to be educated on quality of materials prior to purchasing a home," one individual highlighted. "There's too many people doing DIY fixes that people think 'look nice' but are expensive to rehab and correct."

‌



Another TikTok user recommended: "If you bought a newer build check if the neighbours had this issue!

We had the same exact thing - LVP slapped onto concrete with no moisture barrier causing issues and it turns out everyone in the neighborhood was having the floors replaced by the builder. We got a settlement to replace the floors ourselves."

A third person contributed: "Had this as well... not to this extent though. You got puddles man? You're going to need more than just an underlayment."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

While a fourth exclaimed: "I'm genuinely afraid that's what is happening in my house. Ugh! Now I'm gonna have to pull up a piece and see what we find."

According to Bayland Flooring, meanwhile, amongst the most significant disadvantages of laminate is its vulnerability to moisture.

‌



The firm explains: "Unlike hardwood that can be dried and refinished, laminate's layered composition makes it highly susceptible to warping and staining when wet.

"The longer the water sits, the more it can seep between the cracks, causing the boards to swell, buckle, and even grow mould."

The key is to act fast at the first sign of moisture. Some warning signs that your laminate is taking on water include:

Article continues below

Cupping or crowning planks

Bulging seams

Discolored or spongy-feeling spots

A musty, damp odour

Yet DIY drying isn't always sufficient, as Bayland Flooring detailed further: "In severe cases where the water has saturated the laminate for an extended period, a professional touch may be necessary.

"Laminate that has absorbed substantial moisture often needs to be removed to allow the subfloor to completely dry out. Attempting to dry soaked laminate in place can trap water and encourage mold and mildew growth."

News.title: Ricky Gervais backs plan to rescue 2,000 dogs used in cruel lab tests
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Ricky Gervais backs plan to rescue 2,000 dogs used in cruel lab tests

Up to 2,000 activists plan an “open rescue” of 2,000 Beagles from America's Ridglan Farms, backed by Ricky Gervais, as campaigners cite alleged cruelty

View 3 Images Ricky Gervais has backed plans for what organisers say will be the biggest “Open Rescue” in history, calling for 2,000 Beagles to be freed from Ridglan Farms (Image: Joseph Sinclair/FLOE )

Ricky Gervais has thrown his support behind plans by up to 2,000 activists to carry out the largest “Open Rescue” in animal welfare history.

‌



Campaigners in the US hope to remove 2,000 Beagles from Ridglan Farms, a breeding facility that supplies laboratories. After Life star and animal rights activist Ricky backed the action planned for April 19. “Dogs are the most sensitive, loyal and loving companions any human could ever encounter,” he said.

‌



“I'm appalled that Beagles are bred for cruel laboratory experiments, which are also, today, widely reported to be failing humans too. It's time to release the dogs at Ridglan Farms, so they can live out their days surrounded by the love and freedom they so desperately need and deserve.”

‌



View 3 Images Ricky Gervais said the dogs “so desperately need and deserve” love and freedom as activists prepare for a mass rescue (Image: Joseph Sinclair/FLOE )

Ricky Gervais makes heartbreaking plea to stop separating people from their pets READ MORE :

Ricky Gervais reveals plans for next stand-up tour including title to annoy his critics READ MORE :

The mass action is being publicised in advance as an “Open Rescue, with nothing to hide”, with campaigners arguing they have a legal basis under Wisconsin law to remove the animals if cruelty can be demonstrated. Activists claim the dogs are being held in 2 x 4 foot cages for years at a time and bred for laboratory testing.

‌



Organisers in the US say the legal case for the rescue has been set out by lawyer Wayne Hsiung, who argues Wisconsin’s law allows animals to be treated as “unclaimed” if their owners are implicated in criminal abuse.

Campaigners claim this removes a property owner’s legal interest in animals and permits their removal.

Ridglan Farms has faced scrutiny from legal figures in recent years.

‌



Dane County Circuit Court Judge Rhonda Lanford appointed a special prosecutor to investigate the facility in January last year.

Former federal prosecutor Bonnie Klapper issued a criminal referral in March 2024 alleging illegal surgeries, including vocal cord mutilation and “cherry eye” removal without anaesthesia or qualified veterinarians.

Campaigners also cite undercover footage which they claim shows dogs experiencing fear, pain and psychological distress.

‌



The Beagles are bred to produce puppies for laboratory experiments, which activists argue often involve force-feeding chemicals for extended periods before the animals are killed.

They also highlight comments from Food and Drug Administration chief Marty Makary, who said in a video published on March 18, 2026: “90% of drugs that pass on animal testing do not pass in human testing, when it comes to safety and efficacy”.

View 3 Images Peter Egan (left) added his support along with Ricky for the planned action, describing conditions at Ridglan Farms as “appalling” and urging the release of the Beagles into permanent homes (Image: Peter Egan)

Article continues below

Support for the planned rescue has also come from Downton Abbey star Peter Egan, who said: “I'm impressed with the careful legal case lawyer Wayne Hsiung makes, for the right to rescue the 2,000 Beagles locked up at animal testing breeder, Ridglan Farms.

“There is a history of legal experts ruling that Ridglan is in violation of animal cruelty laws, including conducting painful surgery on their dogs without anaesthesia, or the presence of qualified veterinarians. It is appalling that the dogs at Ridglan Farms are locked into in 2x4 foot cages, many for several years at a time. This laboratory dog breeder needs to stop its cruel business, and allow all of its dogs to be released into happy, loving forever homes, so that these Beagles can live out the rest of their lives in pain-free peace.”

Ridglan Farm has been approached for comment.

News.title: SHARON GRAHAM: 'Workers can’t keep paying for every crisis - we need a plan, now'
News.content:
Workers can’t keep paying for crisis after crisis they did not create. As American and Israeli bombs landed on Tehran, energy bills in Britain are forecast to hit almost £2,000 a year this summer.

In this global world, war in one continent affects virtually every other. No one will escape Trumpflation, particularly those countries that have offshored their oil and energy supply, like us. Decades of sell offs and underinvestment mean that we rely on others. Over 40% of our power supplies come from abroad and we are reliant on imports for food.

This week Britain’s gas market has pushed past three-year highs. In the 1980’s we were near self-sufficiency. But as British workers prepare themselves for summer hikes to their bills, some are doing very well out of war and oil shocks.

Investment bank Jefferies estimates that American oil producers will generate an extra $5 billion in March alone. Analysis by EnergyFlux found exporters and traders of American liquefied natural gas are set to earn nearly $1 billion more per week based on higher prices.

‌



View 5 Images Disruption to petrol supplies due to the Middle East war (Image: PA)

Unite has been warning about rampant profiteering for years, but up to now no politician has been willing to say out loud what most people think – why should profits be protected but not household bills or wages? Coming late to the party, profit caps are now being called for in Europe, as politics tries to catch up.

Trump’s illegal war is just the latest in a long line of crisis that has left the super-rich richer and everyone else paying more for less. At each turn there are winners and losers. The 2008 global banking crash saw the City firms that caused the crash bailed out, while workers’ wages stagnated. City bankers have now even got their bonuses back. A safety net for the wealthy, the law of the jungle for the rest.

A decade later, over 500 health and social workers lost their lives during Covid. We proved that huge numbers of firms had profiteered while prices soared and workers paid the ultimate price when we needed them most. And what thanks have NHS workers and doctors got in return? Attacks from Labour politicians for standing up for themselves after years of real terms pay cuts.

‌



How about the profiteers? Not a mention. In 2022 the Russian invasion of Ukraine, saw the same pattern repeated. As inflation continued to spike, the Bank of England told us all to take a wage cut, while plundering big business ripped us off. Food prices up 38%, wages under attack.

View 5 Images Sharon Graham, general secretary of Unite the Union (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

Now, yet more profiteering is set to put pressure on prices again. Where do workers come first? Crisis after crisis and the same old story. The system is rigged and workers rightly feel it does not work for everyday people. The global system is more exposed than ever to shocks and our higher personal debts - taken on because wages stood still and housing prices rocketed - have made us all more vulnerable.

All of this has led to the end of the old Labour voting tribe. The Government’s failure to improve the living conditions of workers, has cemented the exodus. The longer it goes on, the less likely it is that workers will ever return. As a trade union movement, we cannot just stand by and watch while the people we represent pay for crisis after crisis. We must now reckon with a new political reality and ensure that, for us, workers come first.

‌



Need Net Zero policy to work for everyone

The surge in oil and gas prices has shone the brightest spotlight on the Government’s stance on our North Sea reserves.

To be clear, my Union supports Net Zero but not a jobless transition, based on a random undefined timeline. We need a real plan for what comes next before issuing bans on drilling. We cannot accept a jobs slaughter and put at risk what remains of our energy security. We are already dependent on imports for our power needs, as we are for so much else, so this is part of a wider issue about our national infrastructure.

View 5 Images Oil platform in the North Sea (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

At a time of global change we need to secure, own and invest in our critical assets. Things that we all rely on. Like our energy reserves, like our steel production and like our water system. All are vital to our everyday lives but are owned by overseas investors. It is time to invest in Britain.

‌



Proud of what unions do for our workforces

When I was elected General Secretary of Unite over 4 years ago, I promised to get my Union back to the workplace.

That does not mean we do not “do politics”. In fact, I am probably one of Keir Starmer’s biggest critics when bad decisions affect my members, although I don’t use my members as shock troops in the Labour Party. I’m much more interested in doing what it says on the Union tin. Fighting for workers.

View 5 Images Sharon Graham attends the 'Together Against The Far Right' rally on March 28, 2026 in London. (Image: Getty Images)

So far, since my election, we have put over £630 million back into the pockets of Unite members from successful disputes alone. This is what a trade union is for. Fighting for better jobs, pay and conditions.

‌



Getting rid of state pension helps nobody

At the moment, the argument is being made by some that the ‘wealthier’ should be cut out of state pensions.

It sounds plausible until you think about it. Over time more and more people would be cut out of the state pension system as politicians look for easy fixes. In ten years, it wouldn’t just be the government determined ‘wealthier’ excluded, those on average earnings, would almost certainly be asked to take the hit.

Over time the state pension would become a poor benefit for those much less well off. The political pressure to increase it or keep the lock, would be weakened and many of those no longer benefitting would start to question whether their taxes should be spent on it at all. Universal benefits mean that everyone has a stake, if that principle is ever lost, don’t be surprised if the poor just get poorer.

Wave a banner for all protests

The Governments attack on the right to protest and on jury trials should concern us all. The right to protest is a fundamental right, not a privilege as some seem to think it should be. It is a cornerstone of our democracy.

‌



A crackdown on dissent is almost always a sign of weakness not strength, and political interference in policing of protest has a long and painful history. Moves to try and stop protest and cut trial by jury are dangerous at a time of growing instability.

News.title: Harry in brutal two-word blast at Sentebale charity defamation action
News.content:
Harry in brutal two-word blast at Sentebale charity defamation action

The Duke of Sussex is being sued by a charity he helped co-found in 2006 in honour of Princess Diana over what representatives have called an alleged 'adverse media campaign'

View 4 Images Prince Harry issued a defiant two-word statement following news of the lawsuit on Friday (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Prince Harry has blasted a lawsuit from Sentebale, a charity he co-founded, “offensive” and “damaging” in a defiant statement questioning the legal action.

The organisation, which Harry helped found in 2006 in honour of his late mother, Princess Diana, provides assistance for young people in Botswana and Lesotho, especially those who live with HIV and Aids. He, and another former trustee, Mark Dyer, are being pursued by the charity for an alleged "adverse media campaign" representatives have claimed caused disruption and "reputational harm".

In a statement issued following news of the action on Friday night, a spokesperson for the Prince and Mr Dyer said the pair "categorically reject" the claims from Sentebale.

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s Australia tour IS being funded in part by taxpayers READ MORE :

Prince Harry sued for defamation by Sentebale charity he co-founded READ MORE :

View 4 Images Prince Harry founded the charity in 2006 (Image: PA)

The spokesperson said: “As Sentebale’s co-founder and a founding trustee, they categorically reject these offensive and damaging claims. It is extraordinary that charitable funds are now being used to pursue legal action against the very people who built and supported the organisation for nearly two decades, rather than being directed to the communities the charity was created to serve.”

The statement was issued following one from the charity's trustees and executive director stating the aim of the court case was "intervention, protection, and restitution".

The charity said: “The proceedings have been brought against Prince Harry and Mark Dyer, identified through evidence as the architects of that adverse media campaign, which has had significant viral impact and triggered an onslaught of cyberbullying directed at the charity and its leadership."

View 4 Images Prince Harry is being sued by the charity he co-founded. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

“Sentebale has experienced the adverse media campaign as false narratives circulated through the media about the charity and its leadership, attempts to undermine its relationships with staff, existing and prospective partners, and the forced diversion of leadership time and resources into managing a reputational crisis not of the charity’s making.

“The charity should not continue to use its resources to manage and address the damage this adverse media campaign has caused to its operations and partnerships. This must stop. The board and executive director have taken this legal action to secure that protection. The costs of doing so are met entirely by external funding and no charitable funds have been used.”

Sentebale's claim, according to HM Courts and Tribunals Service, was filed on March 24 - but there are no additional details about the suit.

The trustees said legal costs for the action are being taken care of "entirely by external funding and no charitable funds have been used".

View 4 Images The Prince and other trustees got into a public dispute with Sentebale chair Sophie Chandauka (Image: PA)

The Duke of Sussex and other trustees, including fellow founder Prince Seeiso left the charity in March 2025. Their departure followed a bitter boardroom dispute with Sentebale chair Sophie Chandauka, with reports suggesting that a dispute had developed over fundraising.

It was also reported at the time that disagreements about fundraising had fuelled divisions within the charity, and accusations of poor behaviour led to an investigation by the Charity Commission.

Article continues below

Following the conclusion of that investigation in 2025, however, the watchdog found that there was blame on all sides, and criticised the public spat. Charity Commission chief executive David Holdsworth said in his own statement that the public-facing nature of the dispute had enabled a "damaging dispute to harm the charity's reputation"

He said: "Sentebale's problems played out in the public eye, enabling a damaging dispute to harm the charity's reputation, risk overshadowing its many achievements, and jeopardising the charity's ability to deliver for the very beneficiaries it was created to serve."

News.title: 'Men bullied me for being 6ft7in tall but my bank balance shows I got best revenge'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: 'Men bullied me for being 6ft7in tall but my bank balance shows I got best revenge'

Amira Evans, 26, from Bristol, said men would bully her for being so tall when she was growing up; however, now she's got her revenge and it's proven by her bank balance

View 3 Images Amira Evans managed to get the best revenge (Image: Amira Evans)

A woman who was bullied due to her height appears to have got the best revenge on the men who used to torment her, as she's bravely opened up about what it's like to be 6ft7in tall. Amira Evans, 26, from Bristol, admitted she was bullied "a lot" when she was growing up, but now it appears she's had the last laugh.

‌



When she was at school, Amira admitted she was super slim as she was athletic, but she was also the tallest girl there, and towered over many of the boys. Back then they would "tease her" but now, standing at a proud 6ft7in with over a million Instagram followers, she has reclaimed her power in a way you'd least expect.

‌



Recently, she opened up about how men now can't get enough of her long legs. In fact, there are married men who struggle not to stare.

‌



Now Amira has a thriving webcamming career. Even though she felt "lanky" for years, the job has allowed her to become more confident, as paying subscribers are "kind and sweet" about her body. Despite the fact that a lot of her clients are married, the process has enabled her to love herself more.

When asked why she thinks a lot of the men who work with her are married, she said: "They are always chasing the opposite of what they’ve got. E.g. a tall curvy woman compared to their petite wife.

"It used to make me feel a little guilty, but now I understand that if I am not able to provide the fantasy for them, they will simply look elsewhere."

‌



When asked about why she thinks these men reach out to her, she added: "Many of these men do not communicate their deepest kinks and fantasies to their partners out of fear of being judged or causing an argument. Perhaps they have tried to bring up their fantasies in the past and this has caused a lot of tension in their relationship.

"I think that's why they keep it a secret and search for other options to fulfil their needs, fantasies and fetishes. I am helping these men to understand that their kinks and fantasies are not taboo and are very common, and they should not be ashamed.

"Like I said, if it’s not me providing the service, they will just look elsewhere, and maybe not have such a good experience."

‌



3 View 3 Images She said men now love her long legs (Image: Amira Evans) 3 View 3 Images Amira is now in a much better position financially (Image: Amira Evans)

As someone who felt so worried about her image growing up, Amira has been able to reclaim her power through her profession. Not to mention, since she started making saucy content online, she's earnt thousands.

‌



Her unconventional job has taught her a lot more about what men deem beautiful. According to her, they have all different sorts of wants and desires, even though their wives may not be aware of this.

Naturally this means there are pros and cons to her job, which is something she is quite open about. Amira explained: "The best parts are of course getting paid - the earnings are incredible and have given me a life I could only dream of.

"The cons are the constant trolling on social media, the negative feedback from women and the men who want to waste my time. They think I can fulfil their fantasies for free!"

Article continues below

Even though she's aware some of the men are married, she also admits this doesn't mean they want to leave their partners in any way. It does have an impact on how she's come to view modern relationships though.

Amira added: "A lot of these men aren’t necessarily looking to leave their wife. They’re looking for an outlet. Somewhere they can drop the ‘proper man’ act and be vulnerable - or submissive - without judgement.

"When you realise how many ‘normal’ married men are living these secret lives, it changes how you see relationships."

News.title: Prince William 'eyes dark horse royal' for senior role amid monarchy turmoil
News.content:
Prince William 'eyes dark horse royal' for senior role amid monarchy turmoil

The Prince of Wales could be considering a 'slimmed-down monarchy' when he becomes King, and may look to the next generation of royals to step up

View 3 Images Prince William is believed to be considering reducing the number of working royals (Image: Getty Images)

Prince William may be considering a fresh generation of senior working royals, according to one expert, as he seemingly finds himself "running out of royals" to represent the Firm. Many have speculated that when the Prince of Wales ascends the throne, he will introduce a new chapter for the Royal Family, featuring a "slimmed-down monarchy", which will further reduce the pool of senior working royals within the institution.

‌



The roster of working royals has already been substantially reduced, with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle quitting their royal duties for life in the US in 2020, and Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor banished from public life.

‌



Peter Phillips fiancé Harriet Sperling's secret life from NHS nurse to new royal bride READ MORE :

View 3 Images Prince William could be considering a slimmed-down monarchy when he ascends the throne (Image: WireImage)

‌



According to the Daily Mail's Christopher Wilson, William may be considering deploying Lady Louise Windsor - the daughter of Prince Edward and Sophie, the Duchess of Edinburgh - in a more prominent capacity.

Reflecting on how few working royals have been visible in recent months, Mr Wilson told the publication: "That leaves dark-horse contender Lady Louise Windsor, 22, who charms all who meet her and could be a decorative and useful asset to the royal team. But her mother Sophie, vastly protective of her daughter, is just as likely to want her to stay out of the spotlight."

The royal expert also discussed Lady Louise's younger brother, 18-year-old James, stepping up to a royal role, noting: "Little is known of his character and personality or whether he'd wish to serve as a front rank royal – even if William wished it. Currently he's a pupil at Radley, the Berkshire public school."

‌



View 3 Images Lady Louise Windsor is the daughter of Prince Edward and Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh

Mr Wilson also suggested that William might encounter difficulties as "public demand for the attendance of a royal to mark major and minor events up and down the country remains as high as ever".

Lady Louise Windsor - who is presently studying at St Andrew's University in Scotland, where William and Kate met - has made a few select appearances at royal events, such as Royal Ascot and Trooping the Colour.

‌



Nevertheless, the Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh have been resolute in keeping their two children away from the royal spotlight and providing them with a "normal" upbringing, despite their royal lineages.

While Louise and James are legally entitled to use His or Her Royal Highness titles due to their royal status as grandchildren of Queen Elizabeth II, their parents chose not to adopt the title, hoping it would enable them to live a more normal life.

Article continues below

Duchess Sophie said in a 2020 interview with The Times: "We try to bring them up with the understanding they are very likely to have to work for a living. Hence we made the decision not to use HRH titles."

News.title: Stop buying soggy £7 caesar salads - try the 'dry fridge' hack instead
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Stop buying soggy £7 caesar salads - try the 'dry fridge' hack instead

Caesar salads are the ultimate summer staple dish and we've spoken to chef Jimmy Garcia on how to create the perfect salad ahead of the warm weather incoming to the UK

View 2 Images This is how to perfect your caesar salad every time

After the sun finally made a brief appearance, the hunt for the perfect summer meal is on - and according to the experts, you should put down the disappointing soggy supermarket offerings.

‌



Sunny weather calls for one thing - a huge bowl of caesar salad with a side of fries. It's the perfect meal according to TikTok, either paired with a delicious BBQ or just on its own with a generous helping of roast chicken.

‌



Now chef Jimmy Garcia, owner of one of London's top catering firms, has revealed that the secret to a restaurant quality Caesar salad isn't just the dressing, but a game-changing way to perfect your roast chicken. Paired with crunchy gem lettuce, crispy pancetta and copious amounts of parmesan, this recipe will keep you going all summer long.

‌



While the salad is the star, the toppings can make or break the dish, and has Jimmy has shared two ways to ensure that your dish is top tier.

View 2 Images Jimmy has shared some of his top tips for making a caesar salad

Jimmy told the Daily Mirror: "You don't need many ingredients for a Caesar salad, but if you get good quality ingredients, you don't run the risk of overcomplicating it."

‌



Firstly, you can brine your chicken by submerging it in salted and sugary water for two days, which forces moisture into the meat and seasons it right through to the bone.

Jimmy told us: "Flavouring the water with salt and sugar gives an even season throughout the whole meat rather than just on the skin. It also forces moisture in the cooking time, and makes sure the chicken doesn't dry out."

However if you don't have time, pat the chicken dry and leave it uncovered for half a day in order to guarantee a crispy skin when roasting.

‌



Then when it comes to the bulk of the dish, Jimmy's philosophy is that simple ingredients is always better - but they need to be high quality.

While many people may opt for iceberg, Jimmy thinks it is subpar and that people should opt for Baby Gem, which remains crunchy even when smothered in dressing.

He said: "It's really easy to grow yourself. You can grow it now until September. Just chuck seedlings into your soil and then make your own fresh salad."

‌



Instead of traditional parmesan, try an English hard cheese like Waterloo or Lincolnshire Poacher for a deeper profile

And finally add "really good and crispy pancetta" to sprinkle on top.

As for the dressing, there is one vital ingredient that people shy away from - anchovies.

‌



Jimmy said: "Anchovies give that real saltiness to the sauce, and using them is key. They aren't for everyone, but that salty kick is what makes the dressing so good. Then add in the cheese shavings, either parmesan or poacher and blitz it.

"Sometimes people add quail eggs on top, but in my opinion I don't think it needs it, just a few good crunchy croutons. Simple is always better."

Jimmy Garcia is running a seasonal summer pop up restaurant on the South Bank - Rotate by Jimmy - which opens on 23rd April

News.title: Gold Dancer put down after winning at Aintree
News.content:
Gold Dancer had to be put down after suffering a broken back when winning the Mildmay Novices' Chase on day two of the Grand National Meeting at Aintree.

The horse dragged his back legs through the final fence when leading Regent's Stroll and was ridden out to win by four lengths under Paul Townend for trainer Willie Mullins.

Gold Dancer was immediately pulled up after crossing the finish line, with Townend dismounting and screens erected for veterinary experts to assess and treat the horse but the seven-year-old was put down.

Owners Gigginstown said: "He's been put down. He broke his back. It's terribly sad for the horse.

"What could Paul Townend do? He felt fine, it was just when he pulled up that something was wrong."

Emma Slawinski, chief executive at the League Against Cruel Sports, said: "Year after year we see horses dying at Aintree for people's entertainment and a cheap bet. Sadly, Gold Dancer is the latest victim of this heartless spectacle, which flies in the face of animal welfare.

"The public and businesses should boycott the Aintree Festival, refuse to bet on the racing, and stop watching the ITV coverage and advertising which glosses over the animal cruelty.

"The government needs to act as the British Horseracing Authority and Jockey Club is prioritising gambling profits over the lives of the horses."

James Given, director of equine health and welfare for the British Horseracing Authority, said: "The horse jumped and slipped and lost his back end.

"He came up very quickly and took one half stride to get organised and galloped away.

"I was in the inquiry and gave evidence that looked into the incident - I was able to watch front on and behind - and the horse stayed as straight as an arrow and wasn't deviating off a straight line or being asymmetric, the back legs were following the front legs exactly.

"It was only when they went past the finishing line that he turned around to the left as the track goes and went from cantering to a trot and the action changed and Paul [Townend] became aware.

"He immediately jumped off and was attended by the vets. I don't believe Paul was able to notice that injury at all.

"He would have felt nothing but normal to him and it was only from the action from a canter to a trot he became aware and acted exactly as he should have done."

Two horses, Willy De Houelle and Celebre D'Allen, died at last year's Aintree Festival.

After JD Vance claimed UK electricity prices are “four, five, six times” higher than in the United States, The Independent examined the accuracy of the US vice president’s statement more closely.

Latest figures show the average monthly electricity cost in the US is about $150, roughly £110, while in the UK a typical monthly energy bill is around £79, roughly $106.

Vance also argued that Europe is “completely dependent on unreliable energy sources.”

In reality, more than half of the UK’s energy is produced domestically, reducing reliance on imports and exposure to global disruptions.

Sending British warships to police the Strait of Hormuz is a “fantasy” because the UK’s armed forces are already so depleted, former defence secretary Ben Wallace has warned.

Mr Wallace, who served as defence secretary under three Tory prime ministers, said such a move, which armed forces minister Luke Pollard refused to rule out on Friday, risked “leaving our troops dangerously unprotected and overstretched”.

He urged the government to stop ducking tough decisions and properly fund Britain’s defence, as he accused ministers of “taking the public for fools” after the current defence secretary, John Healey, insisted the UK is ready to defend itself.

Sir Keir Starmer spoke to Mr Trump on Thursday night about the need for a “practical plan” to get shipping going again through the Strait, which is currently blockaded by Tehran, after a two-week conditional ceasefire in the US-Iran conflict was announced.

It comes after Donald Trump demanded that Nato allies send warships to the region in a matter of days.

open image in gallery Former defence secretary Ben Wallace says John Healey needs to fight for more funding ( PA Archive )

Asked about the possibility of deploying the Navy to the vital shipping route, Sir Ben, who served as defence secretary from 2019 to 2023, told The Independent: "These are just fantasies. They talk about troops being deployed to the Strait when they know damn well that they’ve cut their operating budgets.

"It risks leaving our troops dangerously unprotected and dangerously overstretched.

"John Healey needs to get some courage and start being prepared to have a fight with the Treasury and No 10 [for more funding], but also at the same time start being honest with the British public.”

Arguing that Mr Healey’s claim Britain is “ready” to defend itself is “palpably untrue”, Sir Ben added: “The problem is they simply will not make the tough political decisions... So we end up with very hollow platitudes and partisan comments from a Labour Party who think spin is the solution.”

Dr Sidharth Kaushal, a senior research fellow at the Royal United Services Institute, told The Independent that more money needs to be spent if the government wants to “plug many of the under-resourced gaps in defence”.

“Britain is certainly still the beneficiary of strategic depth of alliances, of some pretty impressive niche capabilities within each of the services. But its armed forces are very much in a what you might call a transitional period, where we're moving from an era of small wars to one where large-scale conflict is very much a believable contingency.

“And that process of transition is by no means complete.”

open image in gallery HMS Dragon has been deployed to Cyprus ( PA Wire )

Asked about Mr Wallace’s warnings over a lack of spending on defence, Dr Kaushal said: “I think it's probably true that in order to plug many of the under-resourced gaps in defence, more money than it needs to be spent than is than is currently being spent.

"In certain areas, efficiencies can be found. And this appears to be the bet being made across the services…

“Obviously, there are ways to find innovative solutions to the same problem without necessarily spending more money. But even so, I think the broad picture that that he paints is an accurate one."

While Dr Kaushal argued that the UK could “usefully contribute to an allied effort to open the Strait”, he also warned that there are “definitely gaps” in our defensive capability “that we would see exposed were a decision to contribute made”.

He explained: “Certain things that would have been a part of our offer in the Gulf historically, things like mine countermeasures. We maintained a standing presence in the region of mine countermeasures vessels for around 20 years, which we no longer do because that capability has has entered a temporary trough.”

open image in gallery ( Institute for the Study of War )

“There are also, of course, questions around vessel readiness”, he added, pointing to the long-term maintenance of Type 45 air defence destroyers.

The UK deployed HMS Dragon, Britain’s fourth Type 45 destroyer, to Cyprus after RAF Akrotiri was hit by a drone strike, but the ship took a week to leave Portsmouth as it needed to undergo maintenance - a delay which has been seen as symptomatic of the state of Britain’s defence readiness.

Sir Ben’s warnings come just days after a former top military commander said that the British army is so depleted it could only “seize a small market town on a good day”.

Giving a damning assessment of the military, General Sir Richard Barrons, who was one of the authors of a major defence review published last year by the government, warned that none of the services could do “anything substantial”.

But asked whether the UK is ready to defend itself at the London Defence Conference on Friday, Mr Healey responded: “Yes, and I think what I set out yesterday demonstrates just how ready our forces are when required.”

Pointing to the UK’s monitoring of three Russian submarines found operating in the North Atlantic, the defence secretary added: “Whilst people are rightly concerned about the conflict in the Middle East, we're not taking our eyes off Putin, we're not taking our eyes off the primary threat, and we do have an armed forces that is demonstrating its capabilities to track and deter and if necessary, there are options to respond as well.”

Meanwhile, asked whether the UK could send Royal Navy ships to the Strait of Hormuz, armed forces minister Luke Pollard told the BBC: “Well, I can't go into all the options at the moment. What I can say is we've already pre-deployed some of the Royal Navy's autonomous mine hunting capabilities to the Middle East.”

Pressed on whether Britain would be prepared to deploy Royal Navy ships to the region, Mr Pollard said: “Yes, and as I've already set out, we have pre-deployed some of the Royal Navy's autonomous mine hunting capabilities to the Gulf region already so it could be used, if required, as part of that international effort.

The Ministry of Defence has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Rory McIlroy surges six clear and sets Masters record after stunning display
News.content:
McIlroy sounded without fear about the prospect. “I’ve built up a nice cushion at this point. I guess my mindset is just trying to keep playing well and keeping my foot on the gas,” he said. “Don’t protect it. Go out and play freely, keep swinging. A big part of the lesson from the 2011 Masters to the 2011 US Open was: don’t get protective. Go out there and keep playing, keep trying to make birdies, stay as trusting and as committed as possible.”

McIlroy knows his pursuers well. In fact, he knows Patrick Reed only too well. The divisive American saw off McIlroy in the last pairing in 2018 to don his Green Jacket. And then, three years ago, McIlroy took a little revenge over Reed at the Dubai Desert Classic in an almighty ding dong that involved the American throwing a tee at the Northern Irishman and a feud developing through the media.

It could still be delicious and following his 69, Reed agreed. “It’s one of those golf courses that if you go out and you post a low number, you just never know,” he said. “That’s the thing about this course, when it starts playing this firm and fast. just have to wait and see what the weekend entails. At the same time I love the position I put myself in. Hopefully I can go out and have a good day tomorrow and have a good shot going into Sunday.”

One shot back of second is McIlroy’s Ryder Cup partner Tommy Fleetwood. The Englishman conjured two eagles in his 68 and with only two blemishes on his card – on the first and last – he will be relishing the challenge of going two better here than two years ago and one better than his two runner-up finishes in the majors.

News.title: I wanted to switch my broadband provider. I had no idea what I was letting myself in for
News.content:
The email was offering me an upgrade to ‘Full Fibre 100’, with speeds of up to 100Mbps for the same price. This package was costing me £53.50 a month, and if you think that sounds expensive, you would be correct.

A quick browse on rival Virgin Media’s website revealed that I could get Gigabit speeds, ten times as fast as what Sky was offering me, for £30.99 per month – increasing to £35.99 next year.

I’m a writer, not a mathematician, but it doesn’t take a genius to figure out that Sky’s £53.50 for 67Mbps (or 100Mbps if I upgraded) was a worse deal than Virgin’s £30.99 for ten times the speed.

In Sky’s defence, every broadband and mobile provider is guilty of this ‘loyalty penalty’. While there are consumer protections in the UK for home and car insurance, preventing companies from offering better deals to new customers than existing ones, this doesn’t apply to broadband or mobile networks.

I’ll also say that I received an email from Sky prior to them telling me about the speed boost, which said I was going to be out of contract soon. So the company did at least try to warn me.

A warning to all – expect a lot of calls

News.title: Trump’s war in Iran sends US petrol prices soaring
News.content:
US petrol prices have soared by more than 20pc in the wake of Donald Trump’s war in Iran.

Energy costs surged by 10.9pc in March, according to the US labour department. That included a 21.2pc monthly rise in gasoline, or petrol, prices and a 30.7pc increase in fuel oil prices.

Overall inflation hit 3.3pc in March, the highest rate in almost two years. It rose by 0.9pc between February and March, the highest monthly gain since June 2022 during the peak of the post-pandemic inflation crisis.

The increase in energy prices alone accounted for nearly three-quarters of the monthly increase.

The jump is a blow for President Trump, who has vowed to tackle the cost of living crisis and faces mid-term elections in the autumn.

Surging energy costs reflect a jump in oil and gas prices since the US and Israel attacked Iran at the end of February.

While oil prices have fallen since the US-Iran ceasefire was announced, they still remain high compared to pre-war levels. Brent crude stood at $96 per barrel on Friday afternoon.

The price pressures will make the Federal Reserve more wary about cutting interest rates.

There are concerns that higher energy prices will also spill out to other areas of the US economy. Grocery prices fell by 0.2pc in March, but economists are concerned that they could begin to creep up in the months ahead.

Sports.title: ‘I want to see it again’ – ‘Angeball’ could make shock Tottenham return as De Zerbi vows to bring back Postecoglou style
Sports.content:
THE Ange Postecoglou era may not be over after all — as Roberto De Zerbi wants to bring back his swashbuckling style at Tottenham.

Big Ange’s two-year spell was a wild ride as Spurs soared initially, playing thrilling football and even going five points clear at the top… before nosediving down the table.





His memorable second season saw him win the Europa League, ending their 17-year trophy drought but finish 17th in the league — which led to the Aussie, 60, being sacked.

De Zerbi takes over a Tottenham team in severe danger of the drop with seven games to go.

His initial focus is on rescuing the team from sliding into the Championship but long term he would love a return to the entertaining, possession-dominating days of Postecoglou.

Former Brighton chief De Zerbi, 46, said: “I want to keep the ball. I want to see again the Tottenham I watched with Postecoglou.

“Because in my second season at Brighton, there was Postecoglou here with a lot of these players and it was one of the best teams in terms of quality of play.

“With Pedro Porro, with [Destiny] Udogie, with [Micky] Van de Ven, with [Cristian] Romero and I would like to see it again.”

Lewis Dunk claimed De Zerbi’s exciting but complicated philosophy had left Brighton’s players “baffled” during the Italian’s first fortnight at the Amex in 2022.

Albion failed to win any of their first five games but then flourished, reaching Europe for the first and only time in their 125-year history.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

De Zerbi has no time to waste at Spurs, given their perilous position.

For all the talk of tactics, he insists the biggest change he must make is to his players’ “mentality”, promising not to confuse the squad with any unnecessarily elaborate instructions at this stage.

His big challenge is to lift the players’ shattered confidence after failing to win a single Premier League game in 2026.

None more so than goalie Antonin Kinsky, set to start his first game since being hauled off by predecessor Igor Tudor on 17 minutes after two howlers against Atletico Madrid.

De Zerbi is still missing regular No 1 Guglielmo Vicario ahead of his first game tomorrow at Sunderland after the keeper’s hernia surgery.



But the Italian said: “I haven’t spoken yet with Kinsky as I think he doesn’t need to speak too much.

“I have confidence. He has to be strong but he is strong enough to show what he can do.

“Not more, not less. I think his qualities are enough to play at Spurs. The players believe in him.

“He has to stay calm and confident. He is playing at Tottenham, so he has to be stronger than the mistakes, and to move on.”

He may not have spoken to Kinsky yet but De Zerbi has held individual talks with most of his squad.



That includes skipper Cristian Romero, who is set to keep the armband — despite the issues he has caused on and off the pitch this season.

They include being banned for seven games for red and yellow cards and sniping at the hierarchy with thinly-veiled social- media digs.

Yet De Zerbi explained: “I have spoken with Cristian. I think Cuti is crucial for us.

“He’s the captain, he is maybe the most important player in our squad.

“Like Richarlison, to achieve our goal, we need the best of Romero.”

De Zerbi begins his rescue mission at the Stadium of Light, before home games against old club Brighton, Leeds and Everton — along with trips to Wolves, Aston Villa and Chelsea.



And the former Marseille manager is bullish on his chances of keeping Tottenham in the Premier League — despite their plight.

Asked what gives him such confidence, he replied: “The qualities of the players.

“The guys know the situation is very difficult but if you watch them against Liverpool and also Atletico Madrid in Madrid, they showed their qualities and they showed sometimes the right spirit.

“We now have to show this for 90 minutes and we have to believe in ourselves.

“The most important part in football is the mental part.



“You are used to speaking too much about the style of play, the tactical disposition, blah, blah, blah.

“But, in the end, the mental part is crucial in every work, especially in football, especially in this moment at Tottenham.”

Meanwhile, De Zerbi claimed he was not surprised by the supporter backlash ahead of his appointment because of his support of Mason Greenwood at Marseille.

Greenwood had charges of alleged rape and assault dropped against him in 2023.

De Zerbi described the England striker as a “good guy” who “paid a heavy price” — comments which prompted three Spurs fan groups to campaign against his hiring.



And the Italian added: “I wasn’t surprised. I was a bit sad and sorry it happened because I’m sorry if somebody took offence.

“This topic is very close to me, I’m very sensitive about this topic, because of the person I am and because I have a daughter.

“I have always been against — always — any type of violence, especially against women.

“But not only violence, even just sexist jokes or other sexist behaviour. I have a daughter and I’m directly affected by it.

“I know who I am, I know the type of person I am, so I wasn’t annoyed by the questions — I’m just sad about them.”

Asked if he hoped fans would accept his apology, De Zerbi added: “Yes, also because I’m not going to go back over this topic.

“I spoke about it in my first interview, I spoke about it today and it wouldn’t be right to go back over this topic again.”

Sports.title: ‘There are still things in the air’ – Liam Rosenior reveals whether Enzo Fernandez’s Chelsea exclusion could continue
Sports.content:
DESPITE apologising, Enzo Fernandez will not play any part in Chelsea’s clash against Manchester City on Sunday.

And Liam Rosenior, 41, insisted that there is still work to be done on a “few hurdles” before he makes a ‘clear statement’ on the situation, after Fernandez’s comments about a potential move to Real Madrid.





When asked if those hurdles could see Fernandez miss a massive home tie against Man Utd, the Chelsea boss said: “Not in this moment.”

He continued: “He won’t play on Sunday, but hopefully after that, he’ll be a massive part of the group moving forward.

“There are still a few hurdles that need to be overcome that I won’t go into, but at the same time, I want every player really, really focused now on a huge run.

“There are still things in the air that I won’t speak about now. I have a very good relationship with Enzo, as all of us do, but there are still things that need to be cleared before I make a clear statement on the situation.”

Fernandez, 25, has been one of Chelsea’s key players this season and leads the team in several attacking metrics in 2026.

That led to criticism of Rosenior for suspending him for a huge match in Chelsea’s bid to finish in the Champions League places this season.

But the Blues’ boss stuck by his decision, claiming the side will be stronger in the long run because of it.

Rosenior added: “I’ve had three or four really good conversations myself, with Enzo. He’s apologised to me, he’s apologised to the club, and we’ll deal with that after a massive game on Sunday.

“It’s not about individuals, football is a team sport, it’s not about shooting yourself in the foot. There are certain values and cultures that I believe in, that this club believes in, and it makes the team stronger if you get that right.

“Enzo, I’ve said every single step along this way, I’m not questioning his character, I’m not questioning who he is as a person. I believe people make mistakes, and you can’t overstep the punishment for the mistake.

“We made a decision, I made a decision, and what I want for Enzo is for him to come on here and have an outstanding career.”

Sports.title: Liam Rosenior gives Cole Palmer transfer update after dealing with two stars flirting with move
Sports.content:
LIAM ROSENIOR has been working overtime to get the best out of Cole Palmer ahead of the visit of his former club, and reassured fans over his commitment at Stamford Bridge.

Palmer, 23, has struggled this season with various injuries and is enduring his worst season in a Chelsea shirt so far.





The Blues talisman captained the side in their 7-0 win over Port Vale, though, which was their first victory in the last four matches.

And with a tough Premier League run-in, Rosenior, 41, admitted he has been on a quest to find out how to get the best from Palmer in a bid for Champions League qualification next season.

Asked how he can get more out of Palmer, Rosenior said: “You give him confidence. You point out the things he’s doing well. You point out the things that are still very, very positive in his game.

“In terms of chance creation, I’ve gone through the stats. The chances he’s created in our difficult times were very, very high for the league. We just didn’t take the chances that he created. I showed him that.



“You can over-analyse at times, but that’s not what I want Cole to do.

“Cole’s an intuitive player. He needs to be free to express himself to the best of his ability.

“How we have tried to manage Cole before this period is that there were question marks about why he was coming off, why he wasn’t starting games. We wanted him fresh for this period, and so far, he looks really, really good for that.”

In January, SunSport revealed that Palmer would be open to a move away from Chelsea and could be tempted back to Manchester United in the summer window.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And with comments from Enzo Fernandez and Marc Cucurella in recent weeks about potential moves to Spain, Rosenior highlighted Palmer’s commitment to the Blues, including playing through injury at times.

Rosenior added: “I have to give Cole so much credit because he’s put himself up to play for this club, maybe at times where other players wouldn’t.

“A lot of people speak about Cole’s commitment to this club, how much he buys into what we’re doing. He’s fully invested in what we do, in many ways. I’m really, really delighted with him. Just him as a player, as a character, what he stands for, what he wants to achieve.

“He’s going to be a huge part of things for me and the years to come.”



Chelsea, in pursuit of a place in the Premier League top five, have got an extremely difficult run-in.

They face Manchester City on Sunday, before Man Utd visit the following week, with games still to come against Liverpool and Brighton away too.

Their record in games against the ‘big six’, since the club was taken over by BlueCo in 2023, is diabolical and has taken a huge hit.

And to pile on the pessimism of Chelsea fans, they haven’t beaten Manchester City since the 2021 Champions League final, a stretch of 12 matches without a win.
